Chapter 8: Re-romanticizing the Relationship.
As couples move forward on their journey of healing and growth, it’s so easy to slip into problem-solving mode... and forget about the spark that drew you together in the first place.
Re-romanticizing your relationship is all about intentionally bringing back that sense of wonder, playfulness, and affection that can fade over time.
Now, this isn’t about trying to relive those first days of infatuation. Instead, it’s choosing to see your partner with fresh eyes, right where you are.
What does that look like in real life? Well, it starts with the little things—like showing gratitude for specific ways your partner shows up for you, whether it’s something big or just a small gesture that made your day a little brighter.
You might plan a surprise date or do something thoughtful—no need for grand gestures; even a simple act can go a long way.
Another great idea? Revisit memories you share together. Maybe flip through old photos or take a walk in that spot you both love. Bringing up those moments reminds you of the journey you’ve shared.
And don’t be afraid to try something new together. Exploring a new activity can add a little adventure and excitement, shaking up your routine in the best way.
Here’s a helpful way to think about it: romance is a little like a fire. If you just leave it alone, it’ll start to fade. But with some regular attention and a bit of creativity, you can get those flames burning bright again.
Re-romanticizing doesn’t mean you’re ignoring the tough stuff or pretending everything’s perfect. It’s about finding a balance—doing the work to grow, but also making space for joy and connection.
When you let in more fun, affection, and play, you remind yourselves why you chose each other in the first place—and that’s where real, lasting connection begins to thrive.
